research_question: Among adults with lateral elbow pain (tennis elbow/lateral epicondylalgia), what is the effect at the first end-of-treatment assessment of manual therapy, prescribed exercise, or their combination, compared with minimal or no intervention, on mean pain intensity?
treatment_label: Manual therapy (manipulation, mobilisation, or soft-tissue techniques), prescribed exercise, or combined manual therapy plus exercise
control_label: Minimal or no intervention (wait-and-see, advice only, stretching/advice without an active exercise programme, placebo or sham, or usual GP care)
outcome_description: Mean pain intensity on a 0–10 scale at the first assessment at the end of the intervention period (typically 6–8 weeks), using the trial's primary pain measure when identified; otherwise use the most relevant reported measure among pain at rest, pain with activity, or pain during maximum grip. Extract mean, SD, and number analysed per arm. Prefer end-of-intervention values; if only mean change and SD of change are available, use change scores for both arms and label them as such. If only an adjusted between-group difference and 95% or 99% CI are available, extract that estimate and derive SE as CI width/3.92 or CI width/5.15, respectively, noting use of an adjusted estimate. Do not mix endpoint and change values within a trial. If pain-specific analysed n is absent, use randomized arm sizes or flow-diagram arm sizes and document this. Convert SEM/SE to SD using SD = SE × sqrt(n), after checking table footnotes. Exclude data available only in figures. Do not include later follow-up assessments or outcomes of disability, grip strength, quality of life, treatment success, withdrawals, or adverse events.
positive_direction: For any standardized effect calculation, a positive Hedges g means lower pain intensity with the active treatment than with minimal/no intervention and therefore favors treatment; for the user-requested raw mean difference oriented as treatment minus control, the corresponding favorable effect is MD < 0.
search_queries: lateral epicondylalgia manual therapy exercise randomized trial pain
tennis elbow mobilisation manipulation controlled trial pain
lateral elbow pain prescribed exercise sham usual care quantitative outcome
inclusion_criteria: Original randomized controlled trials enrolling adults with lateral elbow pain, tennis elbow, or lateral epicondylalgia.

At least one eligible active arm using manual therapy, prescribed exercise, or their combination and at least one minimal/no-intervention comparator such as wait-and-see, advice only, placebo/sham, or usual GP care.
Quantitative pain-intensity data at the first end-of-intervention assessment that can be placed on a 0–10 scale or otherwise used to estimate the requested between-group mean difference.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical randomized study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, theoretical papers, and nonrandomized studies.

No eligible comparison between an active treatment and a minimal/no-intervention control; this includes controls receiving another active manual-therapy or exercise programme, an injection, or a drug.

No quantitative outcome data capable of producing an effect size (such as means and SDs, convertible SEs, t/F statistics, proportions, odds ratios, or an adjusted difference with CI); trials with usable data only in a figure are excluded.
Completely unrelated to adult lateral elbow pain or to the specified manual-therapy/exercise interventions and pain-intensity outcome.
moderators_to_extract: Active intervention category (manual therapy, prescribed exercise, or combination)
Manual-therapy/exercise technique, dose, frequency, and total treatment duration
Pain-measure context (rest, activity, maximum-grip pain, or other primary pain measure)
Comparator type (wait-and-see, advice/stretching only, placebo/sham, or usual GP care)
Timing of the first end-of-treatment assessment
Risk-of-bias domains, including randomization, allocation concealment, missing outcome data, and outcome measurement
effect_size_note: Pool raw mean differences with a random-effects model after harmonizing pain to a 0–10 scale. Convert 0–100 mm VAS means and SDs by dividing each by 10. Orient every MD as treatment minus control, so MD < 0 indicates less pain and favors active treatment; invert estimates reported as control minus treatment. Prefer endpoint means/SDs, but use change scores for both arms when endpoint data are unavailable and clearly identify them. Use an adjusted between-group estimate when it is the only usable result, deriving SE from a 95% CI as width/3.92 or from a 99% CI as width/5.15. Never mix endpoint and change scores within a trial. Convert SE/SEM to SD as SE × sqrt(n). Do not leave n blank: if outcome-specific analysed n is unavailable, use randomized arm n or flow-diagram n and state this. For eligible multi-arm trials, include each eligible active arm versus the shared minimal-intervention control and split the control n equally across comparisons while retaining its mean and SD; alternatively combine eligible active arms using standard formulas and use the control once, documenting the prespecified choice. Exclude trials whose relevant numerical results are only displayed in a figure. Assess heterogeneity with tau-squared and I-squared, report the pooled MD with 95% CI, and conduct intervention-category subgroup analyses when data permit.
